title: Merge executor: a GitHub App squashes the allowed checkpoint by compare-and-swap

story.i_want_to: merge an allowed checkpoint to the base branch myself
story.so_that: the merged tree is exactly the tree the gate allowed, with no pull request and no stale head

acceptance_criteria.description: ThreadMergeWorker is unique per story and runs only on a recorded allow for the checkpoint it merges.

It reads the commit's tree from the forge by commit_sha and refuses with tree_mismatch, escalating, when it differs from the recorded tree_sha; otherwise it verifies the checkpoint contains the base head, creates the squash commit with that tree and the base head as parent, records merge_commit_sha, and only then updates the ref with force false.
A retry whose recorded merge_commit_sha is an ancestor of the base head answers already_merged and moves the story to merged.

A non-fast-forward refusal merges the base into the thread branch as the App and records a base_update checkpoint through a control-plane function that has no HTTP route and bypasses the claimant fence; the story stays at ci over base_updated. A merge conflict returns it to implementing over base_moved.
The squash message carries the story id, a one-line printable title, the thread URL and a Loopctl-Story trailer, and no entry body.
The App's credentials are new environment variables documented in deploy/FLY_SECRETS.md; with them unset the worker refuses and escalates rather than merging.

test_cases.name: lost acknowledgement
steps: ref update succeeds, ack lost, retry

test_cases.name: message
steps: build message with a hostile title
expected_results: one printable line; no entry text

test_cases.name: only on a recorded allow
steps: enqueue with no allow; with an allow on another checkpoint

test_cases.name: tree mismatch
steps: recorded tree differs from the forge's
expected_results: escalated with tree_mismatch; no ref update

technical_notes: Forge access through a behaviour with a Mox mock in test.
The base_update checkpoint is written by a control-plane function with no HTTP route, never through the claimant-fenced checkpoint endpoint.
